items.q: I went with Tommy Jones. We went over and played at a little club for about a week... called The Silver Grill

ctx.x: Well, you make the big ones and the small ones. Just like today in New Orleans, right now today, I'll play a little cheap gig and I'll play a big one. But I go on just to keep active. Because you keep sharp on your instrument; whatever you're doing, you're sharp. If you're going to lay around and wait for the big one, the big one might come next year. And in the meantime, you're dependent on somebody to help you over the times. So you just have to determine to exist, until you drop dead. But if you sit around and…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: What were you playing in that show?

I was playing a couple of songs. Something Dave Nelson had wrote. Dave Nelson’s wife, colored woman, she had been with a great show that went to Russia. It was a sensation in Europe around 1921, ’20. Lot of shows, black shows, going all over Europe, being accepted in a civil . . . supposed to be savages ’til they see you on the stage doing that sophisticated [expletive deleted] and change your mind.
